LESSON: TRADITIONAL FORMS OF GOVERNMENT

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: POLITICAL SYSTEMS Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Learnin
Topic 4.1: Traditional forms of Government
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 5

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Traditional forms of Government, part of POLITICAL SYSTEMS Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Learnin in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: howing the governance structure among The Buganda and The Nyamwezi in Eastern Africa and displays them in class. How were communities governed in the past?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Traditional forms of Government together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-Efficacy: A learner develops self-awareness and planning skills as they draw or make a tactile chart showing the

governance structure among The Buganda and The Nyamwezi in Eastern Africa and display it in class.

Creativity and Imagination: A learner acquires networking skills as they undertake tasks that encourage artistic

expressions as they role-play scenarios depicting aspects of good governance in society.

53

Values:
• Unity: Learners brainstorm on the traditional forms of government in Eastern Africa (Buganda and The Nyamwezi).

• Responsibility: A learner finds out the similarities and differences between selected traditional forms of

government.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Social Cohesion: Learners brainstorm on the traditional forms of government in Eastern Africa

(Buganda and The Nyamwezi).

• Safety and Security: A learner interacts with digital devices with assistive technology to find out the similarities

and differences between selected traditional forms of government without visiting prohibited sites.

Link to other Learning Areas:

● Learners use Creative Arts skills to draw a chart showing the governance structure among The Buganda and The

Nyamwezi in Eastern Africa.

• Learners apply English/Kiswahili/KSL knowledge to role-play scenarios depicting aspects of good governance in

society.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Photographs, pictures and paintings, audio-visual clips, Local museums, monuments, cultural centre, Charts, tactile charts,

resource person, approved appropriate print or braille Social Studies textbooks and other relevant materials.
